budget_items.topic: $31,000 discrepancy in the annual town meeting warrant
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee discovered the annual meeting warrant it thought it had approved was changed before town meeting to include an unexplained sum that turned out to match PACC's indirect/health-insurance costs, without the committee being told.

budget_items.topic: Videographer salary increase dropped from November warrant
budget_items.what_was_said: The special town meeting warrant article meant to restore the $31,000 also included a small requested increase for videographer salaries to cover additional meeting coverage, and the whole article was pulled before town meeting.
The station manager reported that six months into the year the salaries line is tracking toward a shortfall, with a firmer number to come in February.
The manager read out the account's ending balance for December, which the committee repeated back digit by digit to confirm.

The manager said interest has not been posted since before September and a Comcast payment received about two months ago is also not yet posted, pending the treasurer's and finance department's processing.
No FY27 budget update was ready; the manager will present it next month ahead of a Tri-Board meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee noted there is no line item for legal fees for FY26, which will affect how the Cable Advisory Committee can be formed/operate; historically such bills came in monthly.

minutes.headline: PACC to seek a meeting with the town manager after being shut out of two warrant changes
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee spent most of the meeting on its discovery that the town changed its annual and special town-meeting warrants without informing the committee, including an unexplained sum matching PACC's indirect/health-insurance costs and a dropped videographer salary increase. Rather than a formal vote, the committee decided to send one or two members to meet informally with the town manager about the warrant process and mutual expectations, and separately heard the manager's report showing a projected FY26 salaries shortfall, a possible move of the studio into the Ritter building, and unresolved questions about the Cable Advisory Committee's FY26 legal fees line.

what_happened.line: The committee found the annual town-meeting warrant had been changed before town meeting to add an unexplained sum, without anyone telling them.
A special-meeting warrant article meant to fix that also carried a small videographer pay increase, and the whole article was pulled before town meeting.
Rather than vote on the matter, the committee chose to send one or two members to meet informally with the town manager about the warrant process.
The station manager reported the salaries line is tracking toward a shortfall six months into FY26, with a firmer figure due in February.
A town committee is weighing moving the cable studio into the Ritter building's second floor.

why_it_matters: This is a dispute over whether a town committee's budget line can be changed on a warrant without notice to that committee -- a process question that could affect how any board's warrant article gets amended.
